Hi, I hope you don’t mind me reaching out so personally, Peter. I’m sitting here alone tonight, staring at our latest reports, and I’m struggling to find the words. I usually try so hard to stay strong and keep a brave face for the rest of the team, but looking at these numbers... **_I’m_** _**_distraught_**_** _._** The truth is, we are much further behind than I ever imagined we’d be at this point. _**_It’s a weight_**_ I honestly can’t carry by myself anymore, and I fear what’s going to happen next. I feel like we’re letting you down and failing the mission we started together. I’ve spent all night trying to figure this out, and I’ve reached the point where I have to swallow my pride and humble myself before you. I wouldn’t ask if it wasn’t urgent, but I don’t know where else to turn. You’re truly the _**_only person_ **_I feel I can trust with the full truth right now.
---

Scott DesJarlais has an M.D. after his name. He ran for Congress in 2011 partly on that credential, positioning himself as the doctor who would fix healthcare for Tennessee. He even sits on the GOP Doctors Caucus.
**And then he spent 14 years voting to take your coverage away.**
DesJarlais voted repeatedly to repeal and replace the Affordable Care Act, a law that extended coverage to millions of working Americans who had none. When the repeal effort stalled, he joined the Freedom Caucus to petition and force the repeal vote anyway. When a revised version came along, he backed that one too, calling it his "number one priority," even after we witnessed protests _for_ healthcare.

---|---|---
His number one priority was stripping coverage from people who finally had it. **This is the kind of corruption we are fighting day in and day out.[Can I count on you to join me?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a03d6349-ae91-4335-98d4-3ea1666eecb1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Pitch in HERE!!️](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a03d6349-ae91-4335-98d4-3ea1666eecb1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This is the man who stands in front of cameras and calls himself a healer. I'm not a doctor, but I know what it looks like when a family gets devastating news in a hospital room and realizes the law is working against them instead of for them. My wife and I lived that. We know what healthcare feels like when it fails you at the worst possible moment.
Nobody in Washington should have the power to make that moment harder. And nobody who has spent 14 years trying to do exactly that deserves another term.
Tennessee's 4th District deserves a representative who fights for your health like your life depends on it. Because for too many families here, it does.

Thomas Massie is gone. Bill Cassidy is gone. John Cornyn just made the list.
[Trump's revenge tour took out two Republicans in 72 hours ](https://us.list-manage.com/_s9HXowFhwP?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)— and back home, Deb Haaland sat down with KRQE and gave the worst answer of her campaign.

| |
💥 **TRUMP'S REVENGE TOUR JUST TOOK OUT TWO REPUBLICANS — CORNYN IS NEXT**
Ed Gallrein beat Massie in the most expensive House primary in American history. $32 million. A nine-point margin.
Massie's concession speech contained a line so ugly even Scott Jennings called it "despicable." We play it.
Three days earlier, Bill Cassidy — who voted to convict Trump in 2021 — finished third in Louisiana. Then Tuesday, Trump endorsed Ken Paxton over John Cornyn in Texas.
Mark explains the one rule every Republican senator now has to follow.
🔥 **HAALAND'S KRQE INTERVIEW FALLS APART ON FRACKING**
She said she'd ban fracking on public lands. Then she said New Mexico drills mostly on private land, so it'll be fine.
It won't be fine.
Mark walks through the actual number — and what cutting that much production would do to the state budget. When you hear what Haaland thinks New Mexico's economy is built on, you understand why she's going to refuse to debate.
---
| [Stream Episode Now](https://us.list-manage.com/GmBgqcLDFlt?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |
🚨 **TRUMP'S LAWYERS SEND DUKE RODRIGUEZ A CEASE-AND-DESIST**
The Dhillon Law Group — Trump's attorneys — ordered Rodriguez to stop running an ad that features Trump in an Uncle Sam hat saying "I want you to vote Duke Rodriguez for governor."
Trump hasn't endorsed anyone in this race. Duke is calling it "political parody."
We break down why this is the kind of rookie mistake that ends campaigns.

🛸 **FOUR ALIEN SPECIES? AN 89-YEAR-OLD PHYSICIST SAYS YES.**
Dr. Hal Puthoff went on Steven Bartlett's podcast and told the world the US has recovered four different alien species from crashed UFOs.
Mark pulled the trailer for V from 1983. You're going to want to see this.

name: Dan Cox
subject: Happy Memorial Day weekend
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Dan Cox for Governor, Nick Krop, Treasurer
body:
Remember those who gave their all for our freedom. | | | |
---
| | |
# Have a Happy and Meaningful Memorial Day weekend.
---
| Fellow Marylanders, Valerie and I wish you a Happy and meaningful Memorial Day weekend. Let us remember and honor the brave American servicemen and women who gave their lives defending our freedom.

Like _Private First Class Richard A. Talhelm_, a 17-year-old paratrooper from Washington County, Maryland. His is a notable story of sacrifice on D-Day. He altered his birth certificate about his age to enlist in the U.S. Army. Serving with the 82nd Airborne Division (same division my son served in), PFC Talhelm was killed in action on _June 6, 1944, and is one of the youngest soldiers buried at the Normandy American Cemetery_.

Or Baltimore-based _Captain Bernard J. Sabatino_ , a field hospital surgeon serving with the 29th Infantry Division of the Maryland National Guard, who was among the Marylanders who lost their lives providing crucial medical support during the Normandy invasion.
**The Maryland National Guard's 29th Infantry Division,** widely known as the "Blue and Gray" division, deployed to the bloody shores of Omaha Beach. Elements of the Maryland-based 115th and 175th Infantry Regiments took heavy casualties but successfully established a crucial inland foothold.

In June 2023 I walked Omaha Beach and the Normandy cliffs with my son and felt the solemn silence, and reflected on the American honor of those who fell in those days. On this Memorial Day, we remember their sacrifice for our freedoms that must be defended.
---
|
---
|
---
|
---
| But our freedoms and ability to enjoy our lives here in Maryland are never more than one generation away from extinction. And today they hang in the balance.

Marylanders are tired of the highest electric bills in the nation, outrageous car registration fees, overspending by $4 billion, and the failed Key Bridge to nowhere from Wes Moore.

I’m running for Governor as the only common sense, real Republican candidate who has actually won elections. **_I’m the only pro-Constitution, pro-life, pro-Second Amendment, and pro-parental rights candidate in this race and together we will win_**.

**I’ll bring back common sense, accountability, and relief to our state and back to your wallets.**

I humbly ask for your vote. Vote early June 11 through 18 or June 23 on Election Day.

Learn more at DanCoxForGovernor.com. ** **

Reflecting on what we've been given and those who gave all,

Dan Cox, candidate for Maryland Governor
_"Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends." St. John 15:13 (KJV)_

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

**Urgent Financial Alert**
A Growing Banking Risk Could Affect Americans With $50,000+ in Savings or Retirement AccountsDear Reader,

Something unusual is happening inside the U.S. banking system — and many Americans haven't heard about it yet.

In recent months, stress inside the financial sector has continued to build.

The government seizure of **Republic First Bank** sent another signal that certain institutions may be under increasing pressure.

According to research from **Klaros Group** , more than **280 banks and credit unions are currently experiencing elevated financial stress** , representing close to **$900 billion in assets.**

For Americans with meaningful savings or retirement funds, this raises an important question:

**How protected is your money if banking conditions become unstable?**

**A Warning From Banking Analysts**
Christopher Wolfe, Managing Director and Head of North American Banks at Fitch Ratings, recently explained:

_"Some banks could struggle to maintain required capital levels, and in certain cases, failures remain possible."_

While no one can predict exactly what will happen next, many experts believe the financial system may be entering a **period of significant transition.**
**A Major Shift in the Financial System**
Another major development occurred when the Federal Reserve officially ended its **Bank Term Funding Program on March 11.**

Some analysts believe this could accelerate structural changes within the financial system — including the eventual introduction of **central bank digital currencies (CBDCs).**

Research from Wells Fargo titled _"Central Bank Digital Currencies and the Future of Money"_ highlights how these technologies could reshape the way money moves through the global economy.

For savers and retirees, this raises an important question:

**What steps can you take today to help protect your savings if the financial system continues to change?**

He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | Urgent Financial Alert A Growing Banking Risk Could Affect Americans With $50,000+ in Savings or Retirement AccountsDear Reader, Something unusual is happening inside the U.S. banking system — and many Americans haven't heard about it yet. ## Gunman Killed near White House
The U.S. Secret Service [fatally shot a gunman](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGvrCAQRn-NdpgBUdaC4jV2-9pXGhYGnXcRDLBr9t_fuNXtbzfJSSbnfP_uy91QoLj-NTvq6tMS8SwBa8W8nBtV3NKz4PqMu4lfFAK6B5ZFgBgZDEzIxRkK70W2TntEgX2Lmis1jVz1MLSbNmayfrqBUNZzUNBLgME9BofcOSd5S_r6BoOQHOAm-k4NN-4tSjmNyoNUjQR0VFPu_ieKdUMf3umFubNpb4Peaj1K0_9pxNyI-TzPLj7sVXHxRsxHClTJlh8nu3Aj5vUZy5ZqYRmPlCs6FtFk9ulmn3CWbTS9HEfF26zdcVIIVMbLad0NhY9D_dVwLy2-AwAA__9JXoPl) who opened fire at a White House checkpoint on Saturday evening, locking down the complex. The suspect, known to D.C. police, pulled a pistol near 17th Street and Pennsylvania Avenue around 6 p.m., firing toward the executive mansion before [officers returned fire](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO6yAQRb8Gd1gwBmMXFK9xl9duaREzBHYxREBi5e9X9i9sN9JI595zv27rzYQY0uO_2VE3l9eER43YGpb18KGhz6-Kj1faTfoJMaK9Y12BwUiZpCBWa0L8rKKz2iECDh1qrtQ8cjUw2Xl9n4QVQiruDLNmm_i0IUjuZmtQ4Wy7oE8akyA4YxMMvZITdxsKMY_KMaGIYGhDy6X_ziE1jy5-8htLv-W9i9q39qxk-EdgIbAcx9Fv6b6dTwLLiSawMHneA4Gl4DOXVml2tPrcKnWhoKUJTaGXL72Ee9_22BVtn0eIMdTxbPHYTYhXavvTVG8NvwEAAP__Fkd87A). A bystander was also wounded. President Trump was in the Oval Office and unharmed. The gunman never breached the grounds, and the FBI is [assisting at the scene](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSgyAYhJ9GOxxEEC0orkmXa690EH7if0HIAIbk7W_MK1y7O7PzfftzXa4aPYbbt95BFReXADV7KAXSUjcssMUjw-0Iuw539B7sCnlhlI2ECsL4YjX698JbqxwAg6EF1Us5j70cqGg3NfQghBnEvBo6GphW4ebRWcomKyVf1xbVuUYF4z2lExs6KabeGeB8HqWjXDacgsUSU_cbMZQNnH_HJ6TOxL31aivlkZvhq2GXhl1qrZ2Lr9Pi7Bt2OfIZnyrk40J8NHcbayDaFUgkb7Fk4jCBJQkeMRWwJIBOBF5gjoJPILsOGWNok7KPit5jHk-s267RfzDKv757KvYXAAD__3cehnw). The shooting marks the third White House security scare in a month, after the April assassination attempt at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner and the May 4 Washington Monument shooting.
## California Chemical Leak Forces Evacuations
Southern California filled evacuation centers on Saturday as authorities worked to [cool an overheated chemical storage tank](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLvOozAQhZ8GOiJ78AUKF9uky7ZbosEeh9kMOAInUd5-xb7CXx4d6Vy-P7fphiy83X_jSqHmMm30OYRqpX36LFxpKa-D7q9txe3BIpRmOiZQ4DplOzBTQpbvZNoUMhFQ31LQ3o9O-17ZdgkEfepJG4o-ZRjVkJ3xzs4peusU2pbDmaYsGK3UAP3F20HnSMaMzmdlfGMUJa5lv_wtvNWFsnzLm_ZLLGsrYan1eTT9rwauDVzxeR44rVPslaNQA9eIwrnsG2MXF1o5onQVt0cnhI8u6jwCRCSV0qwNDNYnDUikhgTJze0e0vPDIny4c859RZb_9fVHzN4B_gUAAP__aeR_aw) and keep it from exploding less than a mile from Disneyland's two theme parks. A tank holding between 6,000 and 7,000 gallons of methyl methacrylate began venting vapors into the air on Thursday at an aerospace plastics facility in Garden Grove, a city in Orange County. The chemical is a highly flammable industrial liquid used to make acrylic plastics. If it leaks into the atmosphere, any spark or flash [could lead to an uncontrolled fire or explosion](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykUL2yqyAQfhrtcHBFSQqK29jltrd0EBbhZoUMkDi-_RnzCqfanfnm-_33WB46UIjbX72jqi4tEY9CWCvm5fChok_vgts77jo-AxHaFcsCHCbGRwZisTrQuYjWKocIOLSoeinvUy8HPrZegTa9MW5a19uohVglR-vEXRpwEoEPbVCXGh9B9JzfYOjkeOudQSHuk3RcyEZwtKGm3P1PIVaPjs70wdyZtLekfK2v0gx_GpgbmI_j6MxarhYX3sB8vQ3Mm84WI9ty-iDbsfqTvkebfJKuyIzHPRhNrOr4ZJQK03FDwovcZmVfRyAKZbrybLsO9PWvvxrto-AnAAD__858g0Q). The initial evacuation order was lifted when vapor conditions improved. However, [the order was reissued and expanded](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0M2u2yAUBOCnwTsi_mzIgkWlyrvbTVV1aZ3AIT69GK6AJMrbV-4rdD3S6Jv5_bF9AGUq9x9woB-pbgVfPeMY2LbXTgP3-uh4f5QDyifljPGGfVNCLVzMXJktAuX3ZqboE6JCPaGX1l4XabWYp907BxD0LTotk0nSXRcHc5IhLlYaHe1E_mwTszJSCKf0xc5OpoDGXBebhLHMCIw0arv8qVTGjim_6xPbJdRjyn4f46sz_Y2plakVbuFccGZMrb9-MrXiE8IDBtXCa4vYOqfeHxh5gEyptkLAA403DzseFCDzAeWTJ6DcmVr7qO3N9EqR6e9Sa6WNM8vUfPx6Uc7Ul1N4P4DyP9H4rxufXv0NAAD__7qchvs) on Friday due to what police called an "unprecedented" event.
## LIST: Best Breakfast in Each State
Breakfast is often called the most important meal of the day, and a new list of [favorite breakfast options in each state](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOszAQBOCngQ5kLzZOChd_Q5e_vRLZeDf4YnBkb4Ly9ifuFa6e0XzSfN3mm4sp7vf_bkPLlOcdj5qQGct8rJFxza-K99e-uf0RU8Lgsc4gYOyE7kDNwcX0mVUbLCECDi1aacx1lGYQul0tXTXpxYxSAVFYJCog7Q3R4LX3QrbRnmtCg5JCXGDojb5IWlCp62hIKNMogSFyLv13jjuvSOmT31j6JW9tsivzszbDvwamBqbjOPoSzqiByRWOS8IGJo-VO1_QPchV7ijn0OEby6er7PhstMWG5xFTinU8yfvmYvol-E-_vC38BAAA__8UT3fo) reveals both classic favorites and intriguing options. In Montana, [the native huckleberry](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHSoyAURp9GOx24osSCYhu7bLulg3qRmyBk4Ronb7-TfYW__-Y7Z86f-3y3FCjuv-2Bhl2aI14lIDPm-fLE6NNZcD_jYeOTQsBtwTKDgKERfQNq3iyFz6zqzThEwK5GI7UeB6k70dfeWLn0ziocLawSrRgBpdSoe7G5YVBDTeb7JnpQUogbdK3ub9KtqNQ4aCeUrpTAjTjl9pEoskcXPumNuV3TUQfjmV-l6n5VMFUwXdfVRsuUog0uZSxc2pT3CiabmdaAFUxIu-fmcdL6af6eWL7r0tglndz4c30GXDBnwlLBVGezvS4KgcrwNdkPS-E_mX-U623gXwAAAP__tXWBWg) finds its way into both pancake batter and syrup.

**Whatever happened to fondue?** For a brief stretch in the late 1960s and 1970s, the fondue pot was the center of American social life. If you hosted a dinner party, chances were good that a small flame was heating melted cheese in the middle of your table. Fondue arrived in the United States through postwar travel and savvy Swiss promotion. American tourists encountered it in Alpine resorts, while Swiss cheese producers pushed the dish abroad to increase exports. The [1964 New York World's Fair](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHO3CAQhJ_G7jjBHpi7wkUad3_alNaeWezNj8ECzujePnKkPEGqkUafRjPz62v-Qg4c15-401h9miO1EqhWynPbuNKW3oXWd9wxfnMI5F5UZpAwCGkE6Nkhh8-sezd6IqB7T6Oy9jkoe5em30ZQSqK0StvBvxbzMA_ltQXzGhx4LXXP45UmDWgl5QPuN3shC2n9HKyX2nZakuOa8u134lg38uGTTsq3Je19GLdaj9Ldf3QwdTC11m4eF3ql9H0BHUwnx4orZVr4oNLBdKRSL_UpujeJhkUUyic5gVXUjURpXIo48OTAKf5z1XPQoqUcXBEeOQuMTuBOmReMRWDtYFL6qYzRxoAdjHnIDqY-j-5oHAKX4dqy7sjhb_f6X4efI_wJAAD__-d1k_U) helped introduce fondue to a mass audience, and by the end of the decade it was showing up in cookbooks, department stores, and suburban kitchens. The concept fit perfectly with the era's dinner-party culture. Young couples entertaining at home liked foods that were interactive and informal. Fondue turned dinner into a group activity. Guests gathered around a pot of melted cheese, dipping cubes of bread with long forks. Variations followed. Some hosts used hot oil to cook meat at the table, while chocolate fondue became a popular dessert. [Buying a fondue set](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFu6yAYRp8Gb7HgB5t4YLiR5S136NIRYfNj02CIDImVt6-coVO3jp-OdKTzfV711fjg4_zfrKiKSzringOWgpveF19wSY-M8yOuJt58CGhHzBootCfanEBoa3x4aVFZ5RABeYWKSdm1THLaVIua6Jmz0YAzo3AjYxSFBOOckXTCrqOVV4eNNiAYpWfgtWzOzE0oRNdKR4UkgqL1JW31V_KxLOjCKz1xq6e0VkEtpdwz4f8IDASGfd9rHM3rgASGPC0EBl8vZQ2EDzredsJ7l6J9IIFLxkLg8vSxmBkJtDqbyRTCe3oMt6WV8P5DvFfZbtlbwvs7cC4aEPXaSFoHxhk_eLK_uFudfpTVpux99yH43B5R82p8eEeUPz3_VPAdAAD__ybnk4Y) became almost a rite of passage for new households. Despite the collapse of the home fondue party craze, the concept survived in a narrower niche. The biggest example is The Melting Pot, founded in Florida in 1975 and now operating roughly 90 locations across the United States and Canada. Today fondue occupies a strange place in American food culture. It is mostly nostalgia. Many people associate it with 1970s entertaining or romantic restaurants. Yet the idea never fully disappeared. Interest rises from time to time as people rediscover communal dining, and some observers point to renewed curiosity about slower, shared meals in a digital era. _Were you a fondue fan with your own fondue set? For a brief stretch in the late 1960s and 1970s, the fondue pot was the center of American social life. If you hosted a dinner party, chances were good that a small flame was heating melted cheese in the middle of your table. Fondue arrived in the United States through postwar travel and savvy Swiss promotion. American tourists encountered it in Alpine resorts, while Swiss cheese producers pushed the dish abroad to increase exports. The helped introduce fondue to a mass audience, and by the end of the decade it was showing up in cookbooks, department stores, and suburban kitchens. The concept fit perfectly with the era's dinner-party culture. Young couples entertaining at home liked foods that were interactive and informal. Fondue turned dinner into a group activity. Guests gathered around a pot of melted cheese, dipping cubes of bread with long forks. Variations followed. Some hosts used hot oil to cook meat at the table, while chocolate fondue became a popular dessert. became almost a rite of passage for new households. Restaurants joined the trend as well (), and a few managed to outlast the fad. Despite the collapse of the home fondue party craze, the concept survived in a narrower niche. The biggest example is The Melting Pot, founded in Florida in 1975 and now operating roughly 90 locations across the United States and Canada. Today fondue occupies a strange place in American food culture. It is mostly nostalgia. Many people associate it with 1970s entertaining or romantic restaurants. Yet the idea never fully disappeared. Interest rises from time to time as people rediscover communal dining, and some observers point to renewed curiosity about slower, shared meals in a digital era.
